front_blocks.md: Define **lithosphere**.

back_blocks.md: The **lithosphere** is made up of the two types of **crust** together with the rigid upper part of the **mantle**; its thickness varies.

cards.front_md: Define **lithosphere**.
cards.back_md: The **lithosphere** is made up of the two types of **crust** together with the rigid upper part of the **mantle**; its thickness varies.

front_blocks.md: Define **asthenosphere**.

back_blocks.md: The **asthenosphere** is a partially molten, plastic-type layer of the upper mantle which moves under high pressure and lies between about **35 and 250 km** deep.

cards.front_md: Define **asthenosphere**.
cards.back_md: The **asthenosphere** is a partially molten, plastic-type layer of the upper mantle which moves under high pressure and lies between about **35 and 250 km** deep.

front_blocks.md: What are the two metals that make up the Earth's solid **inner core**?

back_blocks.md: **Iron** and **nickel**.

cards.front_md: What are the two metals that make up the Earth's solid **inner core**?
cards.back_md: **Iron** and **nickel**.

front_blocks.md: Compare the thickness and density of **oceanic** and **continental** crust.

back_blocks.md: **Oceanic crust** is thinner (5–10 km) but heavier and denser; **continental crust** is thicker (25–100 km) but older and less dense.

cards.front_md: Compare the thickness and density of **oceanic** and **continental** crust.
cards.back_md: **Oceanic crust** is thinner (5–10 km) but heavier and denser; **continental crust** is thicker (25–100 km) but older and less dense.

front_blocks.md: Which rock mainly composes the **oceanic crust**, and which mainly composes the **continental crust**?

back_blocks.md: Oceanic crust is composed mainly of **basalt**; continental crust is composed mainly of **granite**.

cards.front_md: Which rock mainly composes the **oceanic crust**, and which mainly composes the **continental crust**?
cards.back_md: Oceanic crust is composed mainly of **basalt**; continental crust is composed mainly of **granite**.

front_blocks.md: Into how many large tectonic plates is the Earth's crust broken?

back_blocks.md: **15** large tectonic plates, plus several smaller ones.

cards.front_md: Into how many large tectonic plates is the Earth's crust broken?
cards.back_md: **15** large tectonic plates, plus several smaller ones.

front_blocks.md: Which process generates the geothermal heat that drives tectonic plate movement?

back_blocks.md: **Radioactive decay** within the Earth.

cards.front_md: Which process generates the geothermal heat that drives tectonic plate movement?
cards.back_md: **Radioactive decay** within the Earth.

front_blocks.md: According to **slab pull theory**, what drives plate movement in addition to convection currents?

back_blocks.md: The weight of the denser **oceanic plates subducting** and dragging the rest of the plate along.

cards.front_md: According to **slab pull theory**, what drives plate movement in addition to convection currents?
cards.back_md: The weight of the denser **oceanic plates subducting** and dragging the rest of the plate along.

front_blocks.md: Within the mantle there are **______**, which are upwellings of superheated rock that can create divergent boundaries or hotspots.

back_blocks.md: Within the mantle there are **mantle plumes**, which are upwellings of superheated rock that can create divergent boundaries or hotspots.

cards.front_md: Within the mantle there are **______**, which are upwellings of superheated rock that can create divergent boundaries or hotspots.
cards.back_md: Within the mantle there are **mantle plumes**, which are upwellings of superheated rock that can create divergent boundaries or hotspots.

front_blocks.md: Name the four main types of plate boundary.

back_blocks.md: **Divergent (constructive)**, **convergent (destructive)**, **collision**, and **transform (conservative)**.

cards.front_md: Name the four main types of plate boundary.
cards.back_md: **Divergent (constructive)**, **convergent (destructive)**, **collision**, and **transform (conservative)**.

front_blocks.md: Approximately **______** of earthquakes occur around the rim of the Pacific Ocean, a zone called the 'Ring of Fire'.

back_blocks.md: Approximately **90%** of earthquakes occur around the rim of the Pacific Ocean, a zone called the 'Ring of Fire'.

cards.front_md: Approximately **______** of earthquakes occur around the rim of the Pacific Ocean, a zone called the 'Ring of Fire'.
cards.back_md: Approximately **90%** of earthquakes occur around the rim of the Pacific Ocean, a zone called the 'Ring of Fire'.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Volcanoes only ever occur at plate boundaries.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
Most volcanoes occur at divergent and convergent boundaries, but they also occur at **hotspots** away from plate boundaries, where plumes of magma escape through the crust.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

Volcanoes only ever occur at plate boundaries.
cards.back_md:
**False.**

Most volcanoes occur at divergent and convergent boundaries, but they also occur at **hotspots** away from plate boundaries, where plumes of magma escape through the crust.

front_blocks.md: At which two types of plate boundary do **volcanoes** form?

back_blocks.md: **Constructive (divergent)** and **destructive (convergent)** plate boundaries only.

cards.front_md: At which two types of plate boundary do **volcanoes** form?
cards.back_md: **Constructive (divergent)** and **destructive (convergent)** plate boundaries only.

front_blocks.md: At a **destructive (convergent)** boundary, why does the oceanic plate subduct?

back_blocks.md: The **oceanic plate** is denser and heavier than the **continental plate**, so it subducts beneath it, causing friction and heat that melt the crust to form magma.

cards.front_md: At a **destructive (convergent)** boundary, why does the oceanic plate subduct?
cards.back_md: The **oceanic plate** is denser and heavier than the **continental plate**, so it subducts beneath it, causing friction and heat that melt the crust to form magma.

front_blocks.md: What landform is created at a **collision boundary**, and give an example.

back_blocks.md: **Fold mountains**, such as the **Himalayas**, formed as two continental plates of similar density push the land upwards.

cards.front_md: What landform is created at a **collision boundary**, and give an example.
cards.back_md: **Fold mountains**, such as the **Himalayas**, formed as two continental plates of similar density push the land upwards.

front_blocks.md: At a conservative (transform) boundary, **______** are the only hazard, as the plates move past each other.

back_blocks.md: At a conservative (transform) boundary, **earthquakes** are the only hazard, as the plates move past each other.

cards.front_md: At a conservative (transform) boundary, **______** are the only hazard, as the plates move past each other.
cards.back_md: At a conservative (transform) boundary, **earthquakes** are the only hazard, as the plates move past each other.

front_blocks.md: Define the **focus** of an earthquake.

back_blocks.md: The **focus** is the point below the Earth's surface at which the earthquake starts.

cards.front_md: Define the **focus** of an earthquake.
cards.back_md: The **focus** is the point below the Earth's surface at which the earthquake starts.

front_blocks.md: What is the **epicentre** of an earthquake?

back_blocks.md: The point on the Earth's surface directly above the **focus**.

cards.front_md: What is the **epicentre** of an earthquake?
cards.back_md: The point on the Earth's surface directly above the **focus**.

front_blocks.md: On which scale is earthquake **magnitude** now measured, and which scale did it replace?

back_blocks.md: The **Moment Magnitude Scale**, which replaced the **Richter scale**. Damage is measured separately on the **Mercalli Scale**.

cards.front_md: On which scale is earthquake **magnitude** now measured, and which scale did it replace?
cards.back_md: The **Moment Magnitude Scale**, which replaced the **Richter scale**. Damage is measured separately on the **Mercalli Scale**.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Earthquakes at divergent (constructive) boundaries tend to be stronger than those at destructive boundaries.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
Earthquakes tend to be **weaker** at divergent boundaries because the plates are moving apart; they are **stronger** at convergent, collision and conservative boundaries.

**False.**

front_blocks.md: Describe the key features of a **composite (strato-) volcano**.

back_blocks.md: **Steep sides**, sticky **(viscous)** lava, more **explosive** eruptions and alternating layers of ash and lava; they tend to form at **convergent (destructive)** boundaries.

cards.front_md: Describe the key features of a **composite (strato-) volcano**.
cards.back_md: **Steep sides**, sticky **(viscous)** lava, more **explosive** eruptions and alternating layers of ash and lava; they tend to form at **convergent (destructive)** boundaries.

front_blocks.md: **Shield** volcanoes have gently sloping sides and runny lava, and tend to form at **______** plate boundaries or hot spots.

back_blocks.md: **Shield** volcanoes have gently sloping sides and runny lava, and tend to form at **divergent (constructive)** plate boundaries or hot spots.

cards.front_md: **Shield** volcanoes have gently sloping sides and runny lava, and tend to form at **______** plate boundaries or hot spots.
cards.back_md: **Shield** volcanoes have gently sloping sides and runny lava, and tend to form at **divergent (constructive)** plate boundaries or hot spots.

front_blocks.md: Define a **dormant** volcano.

back_blocks.md: A **dormant** volcano has not erupted for many years, but there is evidence of a **magma reservoir** beneath it.

cards.front_md: Define a **dormant** volcano.
cards.back_md: A **dormant** volcano has not erupted for many years, but there is evidence of a **magma reservoir** beneath it.

front_blocks.md: On which scale is the magnitude of a **volcanic eruption** measured?

back_blocks.md: The **Volcanic Explosivity Index (VEI)**, an open-ended scale; the highest in recorded history was a 7 (**Tambora, 1815**).

front_blocks.md: What is a **pyroclastic flow**, and how fast can it move?

back_blocks.md: A fast-moving, very hot cloud of poisonous gases mixed with ash. It averages about **100 km/h** but can reach up to **700 km/h**, causing total destruction.
